title: "Developing a package"

A package developed in a Pixi project has its R, its dependencies and its development tools in `pixi.lock`: the same on every contributor's computer, and in CI. This guide goes through the workflow. [Several environments](environments.html) has more on checking across versions of R.

## Setting up

In the package's folder, set up Pixi, then add what `DESCRIPTION` asks for:

```r
rpix::use_pixi(ide = "positron")   # or "rstudio", or "vscode"
rpix::pixi_import_description()
```

- `use_pixi()` adds Pixi's files (`.pixi`, `pixi.toml` and `pixi.lock`) to `.Rbuildignore`, and setting up an IDE adds `.vscode`, so they stay out of the package's builds.
- `pixi_import_description()` adds `Depends`, `Imports` and `LinkingTo` to the project, and `Suggests` to a `test` environment, which uses the same versions as the default one. Packages that aren't on conda-forge or bioconda are listed and left out: add them with `pixi_add()`, which offers to build them from source (see [Finding packages](finding-packages.html)).

Then add the development tools, to a `dev` feature that the default environment includes, so they're there when you work but stay apart from what the package needs:

```r
pixi_add(c("devtools", "roxygen2", "testthat"), feature = "dev")
pixi_add_environment("default", features = "dev", overwrite = TRUE)
```

## The daily loop

Work in the environment's R, as your IDE starts it once `use_pixi()` has set it up, or with `pixi run R`. devtools works as usual there:

```r
devtools::load_all()
devtools::document()
devtools::test()
devtools::check()
```

Install packages with `pixi_add()`, not with `devtools::install_dev_deps()`, `pak` or `remotes`: those install into the environment without recording it in `pixi.toml`, so a collaborator doesn't get them, and Pixi may remove them the next time it installs the environment. In the environment's R, `install.packages()` goes through rpix.

For a dependency of the package, `type` adds it to `DESCRIPTION` too, as `usethis::use_package()` does, so the two files stay in step:

```r
pixi_add("rlang>=1.1", type = "Imports")    # rlang (>= 1.1) in Imports
pixi_add("github::hadley/emo", type = "Imports")  # also hadley/emo in Remotes
pixi_add("conda::gdal>=3.6", type = "SystemRequirements")  # gdal (>= 3.6)
pixi_remove("rlang", type = "Imports")
```

`SystemRequirements` gets conda-forge's names, such as `gdal` or `pkg-config`, after what it says already. Those are the names tools that map `SystemRequirements` to packages look for, conda-forge's recipe tools among them.

Pixi tasks make the common commands one word, in a terminal and in CI:

```r
pixi_add_task("test", "Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'", description = "Run the tests")
pixi_add_task("check", "Rscript -e 'devtools::check()'", description = "Run R CMD check")
```

Then `pixi run test`, or `pixi_tasks()` to list them.

## Keeping DESCRIPTION and pixi.toml in step

`DESCRIPTION` and `pixi.toml` drift apart easily: `usethis::use_package()` only changes `DESCRIPTION`, and `pixi_add()` only `pixi.toml`.

In the environment's R, rpix notices when `DESCRIPTION` changes, and offers to add what it now needs:

```r
usethis::use_package("rlang")
#> ✔ Adding rlang to Imports field in DESCRIPTION.
#> ℹ 'DESCRIPTION' now needs rlang, which isn't in 'pixi.toml'.
#> ? Would you like to add it?
#> 1: Yes
#> 2: No
```

It says when `DESCRIPTION` no longer lists a package too, but leaves removing it to you, as `pixi.toml` can need it for other reasons. `options(rpix.watch_description = FALSE)` turns this off.

`pixi_sitrep()` also compares them, in a "Package" section:

```r
pixi_sitrep()
#> ── Package ──
#> ! 'DESCRIPTION' needs rlang, which isn't in the default environment in 'pixi.toml'.
#>   Add them with `pixi_import_description()`.
```

It also says when an installed package is older than `DESCRIPTION` asks for. Run `pixi_import_description()` again to add what's missing.

## Compiled code

conda-forge's R comes with its C, C++ and Fortran compilers, and on Linux and macOS with `make`, so packages with compiled code build without Rtools or a separately installed compiler.

- **Windows:** R's build tools also need MSYS2's `make`, `sed` and `coreutils`, which conda-forge's R doesn't bring there. Without them, devtools asks for Rtools. Add them for Windows only:

  ```r
  pixi_add(c("conda::m2-make", "conda::m2-sed", "conda::m2-coreutils"), feature = "dev", platform = "win-64")
  ```

- **macOS:** the compilers use Apple's SDK, from Xcode's Command Line Tools. If a build can't find system headers such as `stdio.h`, install them with `xcode-select --install` in a terminal.
- **Rust:** add conda-forge's `rust`, and on Windows also its GNU target: `pixi_add("conda::rust", feature = "dev")`, and `pixi_add("conda::rust-std-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu", feature = "dev", platform = "win-64")`.

## Checking across versions

- **Several versions of R:** `use_pixi_check_matrix(c("4.3", "4.4", "4.5"))` adds an environment for each, and `pixi_check_matrix()` runs the tests in all of them.
- **The minimum versions in `DESCRIPTION`:** `use_pixi_check_matrix(minimum = TRUE)` adds an environment with R and each dependency at the lowest version `DESCRIPTION` allows, `Suggests` included.
- **Packages as of a date:** `pixi_set_date()` uses packages as they were on a date, e.g. to see whether a bug came with a dependency's release.

See [Several environments](environments.html) for each of these.

## Continuous integration

`use_pixi_github_action()` writes a GitHub Actions workflow that installs the environments from `pixi.lock`, so CI runs with exactly what you ran:

```r
use_pixi_check_matrix(c("4.4", "4.5"), minimum = TRUE)
use_pixi_github_action("check")
```

`"check"` runs `R CMD check` on Linux, macOS and Windows (those of the project's platforms), in each environment that has `rcmdcheck` and the package's `Suggests`, as the check matrix's `r44`, `r45` and `minimum` do: the default environment has neither. Or name the environments with `environments =`. `"test-coverage"` and `"pkgdown"` write the other two workflows a package usually has. Commit `pixi.lock`: the run fails when it's out of date with `pixi.toml`.

## What Pixi doesn't cover

- **R-devel** isn't on conda-forge, so checking against it, as CRAN does, still needs r-lib's [actions](https://github.com/r-lib/actions) with an R from outside Pixi.
- **CRAN's own checks** (`--as-cran`, win-builder, R-hub) run outside your environment, as they always have.
